q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
## Analysis

**(a) Time left until resolution:**
Today is August 22, 2026. NVIDIA is scheduled to report Q2 FY2027 earnings on August 26, 2026, after market close. This is approximately **4 days away**.

**(b) Most likely outcome and why:**

The question asks for NVIDIA's **forward guidance** in the Q2 FY2027 earnings release. This is critical: we are not forecasting actual Q2 FY2027 revenue (which will be reported), but rather the **guidance NVIDIA will provide for Q3 FY2027** when they announce Q2 results on August 26.

Key facts from the research:
- NVIDIA guided for Q2 FY2027 (already known to be issued May 20, 2026) at $91.0 billion ±2%, implying a range of ~$89.2B to ~$92.8B
- Wall Street analyst consensus for Q2 FY2027 actual revenue is ~$91.9B
- This suggests NVIDIA's Q2 actual results will likely beat their guidance or come in solidly within the upper half of their range

When companies beat guidance, they typically guide conservatively for the next quarter. Given:
1. NVIDIA's track record of strong execution and beats
2. Current robust data center demand (the dominant driver)
3. Historical pattern: when a company beats by 0.9B on a 91B base (~1%), they tend to guide slightly conservatively for the next quarter to maintain credibility

The most likely scenario is that NVIDIA provides Q3 FY2027 guidance in the range of **$102-108B**, representing modest sequential growth from Q2's expected ~$92B actual result. This would reflect:
- Continued strong data center demand
- Conservative buffer (2% range is typical for NVIDIA)
- Seasonal patterns (Q3 typically shows growth from Q2)

A reasonable midpoint estimate would be approximately **$105-106B** for Q3 FY2027 forward guidance.

**(c) What would push the value lower (~99.5B or below)?**

- Significant deterioration in data center demand (unexpected slowdown in AI capex cycle)
- Major geopolitical restrictions on China revenue exceeding current assumptions
- Weaker-than-expected Q2 actual results (beating consensus estimates but suggesting momentum slower than expected)
- Conservative guidance due to macro uncertainty
- Supply chain constraints or execution issues

**(d) What would push the value higher (~115B or above)?**

- Unexpectedly strong Q2 actual results exceeding the upper bound of guidance
- Acceleration in AI datacenter spending beyond current market expectations
- Resolution of China export restrictions allowing revenue recognition
- Better-than-expected GPU supply/ASP environment
- Guidance reflecting pent-up demand or acceleration in customer deployments
- Historical case: companies that significantly beat often guide substantially higher

**(e) Base rate or historical reference values:**

The research provides NVIDIA's current Q2 FY2027 guidance of $91.0B ±2% (issued May 20, 2026). No historical precedent for NVIDIA's sequential guidance growth patterns is provided in the research. However, the fact that Wall Street expects ~$91.9B actual revenue (within but above midpoint of $91B guidance) suggests modest beat, which typically leads to modest sequential growth guidance.

---

## Probability Distribution Reasoning

Given that:
1. Current Q2 guidance is $91.0B ±2%
2. Expected Q2 actual is ~$91.9B (modest beat)
3. Sequential growth is typical in strong demand environments
4. NVIDIA historically guides with conservative 2% bands
5. Q3 is typically a seasonally stronger quarter in NVIDIA's cycle
6. Data center demand remains the key driver and shows no signs of weakness

The forward guidance for Q3 FY2027 should reflect approximately 10-15% sequential growth from Q2 actual (~$92B), suggesting a range of **$101-106B** with most probability mass around **$103-107B**.

The range provided (99.5 to 115.5B) has:
- Lower bound at 99.5B (below expected, would imply deceleration or caution)
- Upper bound at 115.5B (above most probable, would imply significant acceleration)

My probability distribution:
- 10th percentile (10% chance below): ~$101.5B
- 50th percentile (median): ~$105.0B  
- 90th percentile (10% chance above): ~$109.5B

Low (10th percentile): 101500000000
Median (50th percentile): 105000000000
High (90th percentile): 109500000000
q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA is scheduled to report its Q2 FY2027 earnings on August 26, 2026, after market close, with an earnings call at 2:00 PM PT / 5:00 PM ET [ifyouspent.com](https://news.ifyouspent.com/en/news/nvidia-earnings-what-to-watch-august-2026).

For Q2 FY2027 (the period ended roughly in late July 2026), NVIDIA's own guidance, issued on May 20, 2026, projects revenue of $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/) [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). This guidance explicitly excludes any Data Center compute revenue from China [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). Wall Street analysts' average estimate for Q2 FY2027 revenue is around $91.9 billion, which falls within NVIDIA's guided range [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). Some aggregators, however, peg revenue nearer $93.5 billion [ifyouspent.com](https://news.ifyouspent.com/en/news/nvidia-earnings-what-to-watch-august-2026). The company also guided for GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins of 74.9% and 75.0%, respectively, plus or minus 50 basis points [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/).
